_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Move image-generation transport behind an approved seam adapter.**

Line 87 keeps direct network I/O inside the pipeline (`deps.fetchImpl(...)`). This conflicts with the pipeline rule set and should be delegated to an approved adapter seam, with the pipeline consuming only the seam result.

 

As per coding guidelines, "Request path orchestration in src/lib/core/<feature>-pipeline.ts must be pure orchestration with no direct I/O" and "All filesystem/network/process I/O must flow through approved seam adapters only; no helper I/O".

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

In `@src/lib/core/generate-pipeline.ts` around lines 85 - 97, The pipeline
currently performs direct network I/O via deps.fetchImpl(...) (assigning to
imageResponse) inside the generate pipeline; move that transport behind an
approved seam adapter by replacing the direct deps.fetchImpl call with a call to
a designated adapter method (e.g., deps.imageGenerator.generateImage or
deps.adapters.imageGeneration.call) that accepts the same payload (spec, prompt,
variations, outputFormat) and returns the response/result; update the try/catch
to call that adapter and consume its returned seam result in place of
imageResponse so the pipeline remains pure orchestration (no direct fetch), and
ensure the new adapter is wired into the deps object used by the pipeline.
```

</details>

The `fetchImpl` dep pre-dates this PR — it was introduced intentionally so the pipeline can be unit-tested with a mock fetch without wiring in the full image-generation seam stack. Refactoring it into a proper seam adapter is a valid architectural improvement but is out of scope for this quick-wins PR (it would require a new seam contract, contract tests, and adapter wiring). Leaving this as a tracked debt rather than changing it here.

The new try/catch around the internal fetch introduces a new error path (network/undici rejection -> IMAGE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE 502), but there isn't unit-test coverage for the rejected-fetch case. Add a test where `fetchImpl` rejects and assert the pipeline returns `{ status: 502, body.ok: false, error.code: 'IMAGE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' }` so this behavior doesn’t regress.

This evidence cannot be from the tree in this commit: `tests/unit/api-generate.test.ts` now contains three tests, including the newly added rejection case, but the captured output here (and the same line in `verify.txt`) still reports only two tests for that file. Because these files are the audit trail used to prove the Seam-Driven Development checklist, keeping stale command output makes reviewers believe the new test was run when it was not captured.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the required Cipher Gate entry**

This change alters the image-generation seam behavior by translating rejected internal fetches into `IMAGE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, but the commit does not update `DECISIONS.md` with the required Cipher Gate entry (`Date`, `Seams`, `Evidence`, `Summary`, `Risks`) from `AGENTS.md`. Without that entry, the seam audit trail cannot connect this new error behavior to its evidence, so the Seam-Driven Development governance record is incomplete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a registered seam name in the Cipher Gate**

The repo instructions require Cipher Gate entries to list exact seam names already present in `docs/seams.md`; I checked that file in this commit and there is no `GeneratePipeline` seam. Since this change is meant to govern the `/api/image-generation` fetch boundary, recording a non-registered seam makes the audit trail non-traceable to the seam ledger and can leave the actual affected seam without governance evidence.
